Posted June 9, 2003

Analysis by Richard Cowan
Cheryl Miller was above all else a very brave lady. She fought both MS and the cruel laws that made her best medicine illegal. On Saturday she finally lost her battle with MS, but her fight to help others must continue.

At NORML's Conference in San Francisco in April, Jacki Rickert and Gary Storck accepted NORML's Peter McWilliams Award for Outstanding Achievement in Advancing the Cause of Medical Marijuana on behalf of Jim and Cheryl Miller. She was too ill to make the trip.
See
Is My Medicine Legal Yet.

I am often inspired by just the strength of people who have to live with great pain, but I am even more inspired by their courage when they denounce the cruelty that denies them and others access to the best medicine, whatever that may be. For Cheryl, it was cannabis, and she did not hide when it would have been so much easier just to keep quiet.

In 1998, Cheryl and her husband, Jim, who is a marvellous human being, were arrested for possession of marijuana after Jim fed Cheryl cannabis in front of the Congressional office of Rep. James E. Rogan, a California Congressman who had gone back on his support of medical cannabis.
See
 Medical Marijuana Advocates Protest
As Congressman Rogan Makes An Even Bigger Fool Of Himself

In 1999, she also went with Jim who was arrested in the Congressional office of arch-prohibitionist Bob Barr. She said that she risked arrest by participating in the civil disobedience because " I' m already in prison in my body. It' s deteriorating and I can' t do anything. At least the marijuana relieves my pain. "
See
 NORML and NORML Foundation News: NJ Multiple Sclerosis Caregiver Goes On Trial in DC Superior Court
and
Paranoia and the Party Line on Medical Marijuana. Who Do They Think They Are Fooling? The DEA and Bob Barr.
and links

Frankly, I have been surprised and educated by the number of people who use cannabis to deal with pain. For many people it is all that works. For others, it reduces the quantity of opiates and other strong drugs that they need, thereby improving the general quality of their lives, beyond relieving their pain.
See
 UK Doctor Studies Cannabis for Pain Relief in Debilitating Illnesses.

The problem of untreated pain is terrifying in its scope and appalling in what it tells about our misplaced priorities. We need to ask ourselves: What is more important, protecting patients or protecting prohibition?

As things stand now, millions are suffering and prohibition is a counterproductive fraud. This problem is regularly reported in medical studies, but it is ignored by the politicians, because it threatens the prohibitionist establishment.
See
 Live Free or Die In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.

A 1995 study found that half of those who died in acute-care hospitals nationwide were in moderate to severe pain.

A 1998 survey of family members of recently deceased people in Oregon found that over 50% reported that their dying relative had moderate or severe pain in their last week of life.
See
 How Time Flies When You Are Not In Pain. Two Articles Document the Government's War on the Sick and Dying.

A Brown University study, published in the Journal of the American Medical Association in 2001, found that 40 percent of nursing home patients nationwide with acute or chronic pain are not getting adequate pain treatment.

In 2002, it was reported that common estimates found that pain was poorly controlled in 26 to 41 percent of all cancer patients. Every year there are more such reports.

Last month, the Journal of the American Medical Association published a study showing that 37 percent of participants in methadone maintenance programs and 24 percent of inpatients in short-term, residential drug-treatment programs said they had suffered chronic severe pain. Among these, half of inpatients and one-third of those on methadone maintenance said they self-medicated with illicit drugs and alcohol.

In other words, a major part of the drug problem which prohibition is supposed to prevent is actually caused by the undertreatment of pain, which is caused by prohibition!

Many more are also dealing with severe psychological problems, but that is another story.

Ironically, some easily available treatments can be deadly. According to the 2000 DAWN -- " Drug Abuse Warning Network " , anti-inflammatory drugs (including aspirin and Aleve ) were implicated in the deaths of 16,000 people in 2000 because of bleeding ulcers and related complications. Of course, aspirin is hardly unique in its dangers.
See
Lethal Dose Of Cynicism From Makers Of Tylenol Poll On Aspirin Dangers
Context Of Medical Marijuana Debate
and
 Meanwhile UK Painkillers Kill 2,000 Per Year. But They Are Sold Over-the-Counter So They Must Be Safe!

Aside from the suppression of cannabis, it is often very difficult for patients to get adequate dosages of morphine or other opiates because doctors are either too afraid of the very real danger of being arrested for over-prescribing, or simply ignorant about how to treat pain.

Doctors who do try to treat pain are sufficiently rare that they often find themselves overrun with pain patients, and by addicts who may or may not also have pain problems. They may then find themselves overrun with DEA agents.

It seems morally obvious that no one should have to suffer untreated pain because someone else might abuse pain relievers.

That amounts to torturing innocent people because of a crime that might be committed by someone else. It was precisely that sort of unspeakable behavior that we are now being told justified the overthrow of Saddam Hussein. It would be a crime for me to carry that line of thought to its logical conclusion, and I am a man of peace, but evil is evil.

May Cheryl rest with the angels, and may those who made her suffering worse not.
